subtitle: When the Iron Emir Emptied the Throne of Delhi

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of mounted conqueror over a hazy cityscape
panels.action: Timur sits rigid on a warhorse, mail and fur cloak catching a pale winter sun, as a distant, smoke-veiled silhouette of Delhi lies before him on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Timur, the iron emir of Samarkand, rides into a broken Delhi Sultanate in 1398, leaving its capital emptied and its glory scattered.

i18n.hi: समरकंद का लौह अमीर तीमूर 1398 में टूटी दिल्ली सल्तनत पर चढ़ आया, राजधानी को सूना कर गया, शान शिखर से बिखर गई।

panels.shot: broad establishing aerial over the Indo-Gangetic plain
panels.action: The camera floats above the brown sweep of the north Indian plains, sparse villages and ruined canals marking the land as winter dust hangs over a shrinking, distant city.

dialogue.text: For decades, the Tughlaq sultans of Delhi had bled their strength away—rebellions, failed schemes and rival claimants pulling at a once-mighty northern empire.

i18n.hi: दशकों से तुग़लक सुल्तान बग़ावत, नाकाम चालों और दावेदारों में ताकत गंवाते रहे, कभी लोहे जैसी उत्तरी सल्तनत को भीतर से खोखला कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a crumbling city gate and neglected fortifications
panels.action: A weathered stone gate of Delhi stands with cracked battlements and weeds in its joints, a few wary soldiers mustering under faded banners of the Tughlaqs.

dialogue.text: By 1398, Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Tughlaq held Delhi in name, but his authority barely reached beyond its walls. The countryside listened to other masters.

i18n.hi: 1398 तक नासिरुद्दीन महमूद तुग़लक नाम भर का दिल्ली का मालिक था, हुक्म शहर की दीवारों से बाहर मुश्किल से जाता; गांव-देहात और आक़ाओं के थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Timur in council tent, maps spread before him
panels.action: Inside a rich Central Asian tent, Timur leans over a carpet, staring at a map showing the Indus and the road to Delhi, commanders around him frozen in attentive silence.

dialogue.text: From far Samarkand, Timur had watched. He saw a fractured Delhi, rich in trade and artisans, yet weakened by rivalries. To him, it was a frontier to be struck.

i18n.hi: दूर समरकंद से तीमूर देखता रहा, उसे दिल्ली टूटी लेकिन दौलत और हुनर से भरी दिखी, रक़ाबत से कमज़ोर—उसके लिए ये एक सरहद थी, जिस पर चोट करनी थी।

panels.shot: three-quarter profile of Timur pointing toward the map’s Delhi mark
panels.action: Timur straightens, his weathered face hard, as he extends a gloved finger toward the inked circle of Delhi on the map, advisers listening under lamp light.

dialogue.speaker: timur
dialogue.text: Delhi is divided. We take its gold, its craftsmen, not its throne.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली बँटी हुई है। हम इसका सोना और कारीगर लेंगे, तख़्त नहीं।

panels.shot: sweeping wide of the Timurid host crossing the Indus
panels.action: Timur rides at the head of a vast column of horsemen and camels, lines stretching over the cold waters of a broad river ford, banners snapping in the winter wind.

dialogue.text: In the autumn of 1398, Timur’s army crossed into north India. Horse-archers, armored elite and camp followers flowed along the old invasion routes of Punjab.

i18n.hi: 1398 की ख़िज़ाँ में तीमूर की फ़ौज उत्तर भारत में उतरी; घुड़सवार तीरंदाज़, बख़्तरबंद نخبة और लश्कर की भीड़ पंजाब की पुरानी हमलावर राहों से बहती गई।

panels.shot: side shot of Timur observing burning settlements from a ridge
panels.action: From a low ridge, Timur sits impassive on horseback as below, a small town near the route lies in ruin, its emptied streets and smoldering houses stretching into haze.

dialogue.text: Resistance along the way was sporadic and broken. Towns that stood in his path were punished; those that submitted were stripped of wealth and labor.

i18n.hi: रास्ते भर मुक़ाबला बिखरा और कमज़ोर रहा; जो शहर अड़े, सज़ा पाए, जो झुके, दौलत और मज़दूरी से खाली कर दिए गए।

panels.shot: tense medium shot in camp, captives in the background behind stakes
panels.action: In a cold camp outside Delhi, rows of Indian prisoners sit guarded behind stakes, while Timur, seated on a raised platform, listens to scouts report on the approaching battle.

dialogue.text: As Timur neared Delhi, his camp held thousands of captives taken along the march. His chroniclers describe a hard choice before the final clash.

i18n.hi: जैसे ही तीमूर दिल्ली के क़रीब पहुँचा, उसके डेरों में सफ़र से पकड़े हज़ारों क़ैदी थे; उसका वक़्त-नवीस आख़िरी टक्कर से पहले एक सख्त फ़ैसले का ज़िक्र करता है।

panels.shot: somber close-up on Timur’s face half-lit, eyes unreadable
panels.action: Timur’s face fills the frame, one side in shadow, as he sits rigid, hands clasped on his knee, the distant murmur of prisoners carried faintly on the cold air.

dialogue.text: Later Timurid traditions speak of a mass killing of these prisoners before the battle, to keep his rear secure. The figures given are vast, yet shaped by rhetoric.

i18n.hi: बाद की तैमूरी रिवायतें बताती हैं कि जंग से पहले क़ैदियों का सामूहिक कत्ल हुआ, ताकि पीछे का मोर्चा सुरक्षित रहे; आँकड़े बेहिसाब हैं, मगर ज़बान से गढ़े हुए।

panels.shot: wide view of Timur’s battle line facing Delhi’s forces under a pale sky
panels.action: Outside the city, Timur’s disciplined cavalry and infantry stand in ordered ranks, bowstrings taut, facing a looser line of Delhi’s forces beneath a hazy December sun.

dialogue.text: In December 1398, Timur met the Sultanate’s army near Delhi. His seasoned formations, hardened by campaigns in Persia and Central Asia, broke the defense with grim efficiency.

i18n.hi: दिसंबर 1398 में तीमूर ने दिल्ली के पास सल्तनत की फ़ौज से टक्कर ली; फ़ारस और मध्य एशिया की मुहिमों से तपे उसके दस्ते दिल्ली की रोक को बेरहम नाप से तोड़ गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mahmud Tughlaq’s standard retreating toward the city
panels.action: A banner bearing the Tughlaq emblem recedes in the distance toward Delhi’s walls, a knot of riders around it shrinking as dust and confusion fill the battlefield.

dialogue.text: Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Tughlaq did not stand to the end. Faced with Timur’s advance and internal weakness, he fled, leaving Delhi to its fate.

i18n.hi: नासिरुद्दीन महमूद तुग़लक आख़िर तक खड़ा न रहा; तीमूर की चढ़ाई और अंदरूनी कमज़ोरी देख वो भाग निकला, दिल्ली को तक़दीर पर छोड़ गया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Timur entering through a Delhi gate with his vanguard
panels.action: Timur rides slowly through a massive stone gate of Delhi, his vanguard close behind, while anxious city dwellers watch from shadowed doorways and rooftops.

dialogue.text: Timur entered Delhi as conqueror, not as new sultan. He saw a wealthy, fractured metropolis, and for days, he allowed it to be stripped.

i18n.hi: तीमूर दिल्ली में फ़तहयाब बनकर आया, नया सुल्तान बनकर नहीं; उसने शहर को दौलतमंद, मगर बिखरा देखा और कई दिन उसे निचुड़ने दिया।

panels.shot: sweeping interior wide of Delhi bazaar being looted under Timur’s gaze
panels.action: In a grand bazaar, carved arches looming overhead, Timur watches from horseback as soldiers seize chests and textiles, merchants kneeling amid scattered goods and upturned carts.

dialogue.text: Treasures of merchants, nobles and shrines flowed into the invaders’ hands. Temples and mosques alike lost their stores of gold and precious objects in the tumult.

i18n.hi: साहूकारों, उमराओं और मज़ारों का ख़ज़ाना लुटेरों के हाथ बह निकला; मंदिर हों या मस्जिदें, हर जगह का सोना और नेमत इस हलचल में उघड़ गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of darkened neighborhoods, smoke hanging low over silent streets
panels.action: A neighborhood of packed houses lies dim under an overcast sky, doors shattered, courtyards empty, thin columns of smoke rising where fires still smolder.

dialogue.text: Chronicles describe terrible devastation in Delhi, its lanes emptied and many quarters burned or abandoned. Exact numbers are lost, but the memory is of catastrophe.

i18n.hi: तवारीख़ दिल्ली की दिल दहला देने वाली बरबादी लिखती हैं—गलियाँ सूनी, कई मुहल्ले जले या छोड़ दिए गए; सही गिनती खो गई, कहानी बस तबाही की है।

panels.shot: medium shot of artisans being selected under Timur’s supervision
panels.action: In an open square, lined-up craftsmen—metalworkers, masons, weavers—stand as Timur, flanked by scribes, calmly points to those chosen to leave with his caravan.

dialogue.text: Timur did not come to sit on Delhi’s throne. He came to carry away its skills. Artisans of many trades were seized, bound for distant Samarkand.

i18n.hi: तीमूर दिल्ली का तख़्त हथियाने नहीं आया था; वो इसकी हुनरमंदी उठाने आया था—हर फ़न के कारीगर पकड़े गए, दूर समरकंद की राह बाँध दिए गए।

panels.shot: long shot of the departing Timurid train leaving Delhi’s ruined outskirts
panels.action: A vast train of carts, laden camels and mounted guards winds away from the shattered outskirts of Delhi, Timur at its head, the city shrinking behind them in the morning haze.

dialogue.text: After days of plunder and seizure, Timur turned his back on Delhi. He left not an administration, but ash, grief and a hollowed capital.

i18n.hi: कई दिन की लूट और पकड़ के बाद तीमूर ने दिल्ली से मुँह मोड़ लिया; पीछे कोई इंतज़ाम नहीं, बस राख, मातम और खोखली राजधानी छोड़ी।

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of Samarkand’s monuments rising, Timur overlooking
panels.action: In Samarkand, tall turquoise domes and new stone facades gleam in clear sunlight as Timur stands on a terrace, viewing building works filled with laboring artisans.

dialogue.text: In Samarkand, Delhi’s captives joined artisans from Persia and beyond, raising mosques, madrasas and palaces. Timur’s capital shone brighter as Delhi’s light dimmed.

i18n.hi: समरकंद में दिल्ली के बंदी, फ़ारस और दूर-दूर के कारीगरों से जा मिले, मस्जिदें, मदरसें और महल उठे; तीमूर की राजधानी जगमगाई, तो दिल्ली की रौशनी मन्द हुई।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of a ruined Delhi courtyard slowly reinhabited
panels.action: Back in Delhi, a cracked courtyard shows signs of hesitant life—few families carry water through broken arches, a lone craftsman sits amid shattered stone blocks.

dialogue.text: Delhi would survive, but altered. Its political center no longer commanded the wide reach it had under earlier sultans. The shock of Timur’s sack echoed for generations.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली बची रही, मगर बदली हुई; उसका सियासी मरकज़ अब पहले सुल्तानों जैसा दूर तक दम नहीं दिखा सका; तीमूर की लूट का सदमा पीढ़ियों तक गूँजा।

panels.shot: reflective aerial over Delhi and the wider plains fading into distance
panels.action: From high above, Delhi’s clustered buildings stretch into the plains, the scars softened by time, while the roads toward Punjab and Central Asia fade into a light-filled horizon.

dialogue.text: Timur left Delhi empty of much wealth and craft, but full of warning: a city divided within stands weakest when the storm rides in from afar.

i18n.hi: तीमूर दिल्ली की दौलत और हुनर का बड़ा हिस्सा खाली कर गया, मगर एक सबक भर दिया: भीतर से बँटी शहर पर दूर से उठता तूफ़ान सबसे भारी पड़ता है।

title_i18n.hi: तीमूर ने दिल्ली सूनी छोड़ दी

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Iron Emir Emptied the Throne of Delhi
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब लौह अमीर ने दिल्ली का तख़्त खाली कर दिया
